reviews.reason: Closing clears the local credential, saved flag and client tab. Opening an instance observes an instance-keyed async credential; receiving a saved key initializes an editable input. The tests restore, clear and save a key; they do not measure transient paints.

Closing resets three independent state values, whereas a saved credential response sets the key and saved flag. These setters do not retrigger the effect. Client tab and restore/clear tests exercise both states; setter count is not a render-count measurement.

apiKey must accept unsubmitted input independently of credentialQuery.data. Save sends the edited value and clear deletes the saved credential. The client tests exercise restore, clear, edit and explicit save.

The instance credential query is enabled by external modal selection and keyed by instance id; the effect consumes its eventual saved value or handles modal closure. A local click handler cannot know the eventual query result. Client configuration tests exercise both hydration and explicit actions.

The installed vditor@3.11.2 dist/method.d.ts declares static preview(previewElement: HTMLDivElement, …). McpCommandMarkdownPreview passes its div ref directly; replacing it with section would violate that type. The client configuration test locates both named regions and asserts the install preview is the actual target passed with its Markdown.

The concrete transformation stages retain meaningful original identity/measurement/option semantics; there is no demonstrated repeated full-source lookup. The parameter map/filter/map captures the original parameter index before filtering; this index distinguishes duplicate parameter names and must not be recomputed after filtering.

McpInstancesTab composes the active instance page and its directory, copy, configuration and edit dialogs. useMcpDirectoryEditor owns the staged graph and useMcpInstanceActions owns lifecycle mutations. DirectoryPagedSelect owns its own search/page; selecting an option does not commit a graph. The paged-browsing scenario follows a selected tool through the explicit mount save.

Debug fields exclude mcp_call controls before projecting the selected tool’s business mappings into typed inputs. The debug scenario sets appId and checks mcp_arguments in both result modes; this is a bounded projection, not a performance measurement.

renderFieldInput returns existing input types under a keyed Form.Item; it is called directly and is not a JSX component type. The scenario edits appId and checks the corresponding request. It does not assert focus or remount counts.

Editable argument values, pending mode, displayed result mode, result and error can change independently. The debug scenario distinguishes missing business arguments, execution requests and the normal versus detailed response. A reducer is possible, not required by these transitions.

This is the composition point for a server-paged tool catalog and the selected tool editor. The catalog hook owns route/query and list actions; the editor hook owns detail, form session and save. The progressive-load and editor scenarios distinguish list mount, explicit detail loading and the actual save payload.

Descriptor projection excludes reserved call parameters; legacy call selection then maps only selected controls into mcp_call entries, preserving ordinary business mappings. Unit tests check migration of an allowlist and preservation of custom descriptions on load/refresh.

ObservePanelQueries is internal to the test provider and only registers its QueryClient for request settling/teardown. Tests import the fixture render and interaction helpers. This is not a browser Fast Refresh entry; exporting the observer is unnecessary.

The useQuery queryFn reads the server page selected by its cache key, not a simulated UI event. A returned total can shrink without a pagination click. Only a completed page whose number exceeds ceil(total / pageSize) (minimum 1) repairs the panel position. The tab-switch test verifies the server page/size contract; the shrink guard is source evidence.

The panel, not the unmounted tab, owns pagination across tab switches. The child passes no rows or local draft upstream: it corrects the parent’s requested position only when the server total rules it out, preserving pageSize. Deriving a display page only in the table would leave the query key on the invalid page.

setPosition is the stable useState dispatcher from the panel’s useMcpTablePagination, not a notification on every child change. No dispatch precedes returned page data or occurs for a valid page. An out-of-range position changes the request key to the last valid page; the extra fetch in that case is intentional.
